textbook:
Clean cutaway textbook illustration of a SINGLE Listeria monocytogenes bacterium, centered in a square 1:1 1080x1080 frame with generous negative space around it for later labels. Semi-flat vector-style shading, crisp clean boundaries between structures, a MUTED desaturated educational palette of soft dusty tints, THIN clean outlines and gentle soft shading. Never bright primary or cartoon colours, never heavy black cartoon strokes.

SHAPE: the cell is a SHORT, STUBBY, STRAIGHT ROD — a coccobacillus — lying on a shallow diagonal from lower right to upper left, only about THREE TIMES LONGER THAN IT IS WIDE, with smoothly rounded, evenly domed poles and parallel sides. It is a small compact rod, NOT a long noodle, NOT a filament, NOT a sphere. Its width is uniform along its whole length: there is NO bulge, NO swelling, NO knob and NO egg-shaped body anywhere inside or on the cell.

THE SIGNATURE FEATURE — THE ACTIN COMET TAIL. Streaming away from ONE POLE ONLY of the rod (the lower-right pole) is a broad COMET TAIL made of HOST CELL ACTIN FILAMENTS. Draw it as a DENSE BUSHY MESHWORK — like a thick brush, a bottle-brush, a bundle of pale hay, a tangle of fine cotton threads — built from MANY HUNDREDS of individually visible, short, fine, criss-crossing, branching filaments in a COOL PALE BLUE-WHITE, packed tightly against the pole and fanning out into a soft cone that widens and frays into loose separate threads at its far end. The filaments visibly BRANCH at shallow Y angles off one another. The tail is roughly one and a half to two times the length of the bacterium and clearly wider than the bacterium at its far end. It is a MATERIAL made of threads, not a beam of light and not a single object. The tail is deliberately a DIFFERENT COLOUR FAMILY (cool pale blue-white) from every part of the bacterium, because it is host material, not bacterial material. Where the tail meets the pole, that pole of the bacterium carries a coating of small gold-ochre surface studs (the ActA protein) which the filaments spring from.

CRITICAL — WHAT THE TAIL MUST NOT LOOK LIKE: NOT a smooth solid rudder, paddle, fin or fish tail. NOT a single thick whip, lash, whisker or flagellum. NOT a rocket exhaust, flame, jet, plume of smoke or vapour trail. NOT a glow, halo, aura or light burst. NOT straight radiating rays, speed lines, motion lines, streaks or a starburst of any kind. There must be NO radiating straight lines anywhere in the picture. It is a bushy thicket of many short fine tangled threads and nothing else.

ENVELOPE — this bacterium is GRAM-POSITIVE, so from the outside in there are exactly TWO envelope layers and NO outer membrane: (1) a CONSPICUOUSLY THICK sage-green PEPTIDOGLYCAN CELL WALL drawn as a broad homogeneous band, clearly the thickest layer; (2) beneath it a thin muted violet PLASMA MEMBRANE. There must be NO second outer membrane, NO periplasmic gap between two membranes, NO shaggy LPS or O-antigen fringe, and NO thick capsule halo around the cell.

CUTAWAY: a quarter of the envelope is peeled back along the upper side of the rod in a long soft-edged window, so the two envelope layers are visible in section as two distinct stacked bands and the interior is on show. Inside: a pale warm ivory-amber CYTOPLASM containing ONE irregular, lobed, cloud-like dusty blue-purple NUCLEOID (a loose tangled DNA mass, never a tidy circular loop or ring), and many tiny scattered teal RIBOSOME dots dispersed throughout the cytoplasm. There are NO membrane-bound organelles, NO nucleus, NO mitochondria, and absolutely NO SPORE — this species does not form spores.

FLAGELLA: exactly TWO or THREE very fine, long, smoothly wavy coral-pink FLAGELLA emerging from the SIDES and from the pole OPPOSITE the tail, sweeping out into the open background. They are single smooth sinuous threads, obviously different from the dense pale thicket of the actin tail. Do not draw a dense tuft; do not draw them from the tail pole.

CONTEXT: the background is the interior of a HOST CELL — a soft, dark, muted mauve-grey cytoplasm with a few very faint, blurred, out-of-focus host organelle shapes far in the corners, kept dim and uncluttered so labels read clearly. Fill the whole square edge to edge with this background. No black border, no dark frame, no vignette, no letterbox bars, and do not draw the illustration as a sheet or card lying on a surface.

No text, no letters, no numbers, no labels, no arrows, no scale bar, no watermark. A single specimen only, no duplicates.
sem:
Photorealistic false-colour SCANNING ELECTRON MICROGRAPH of a SINGLE Listeria monocytogenes bacterium, square 1:1, 1080x1080, centered with generous margin. Crisp three-dimensional surface texture, shallow depth of field, cool studio microscopy lighting, the specimen resting on a subtly textured substrate.

SPECIMEN: a SHORT, STUBBY, STRAIGHT ROD — a coccobacillus — only about THREE TIMES LONGER THAN IT IS WIDE, with smoothly rounded domed poles, parallel sides and a uniform width along its whole length. The surface is smooth and finely pebbled. There is NO bulge, NO swelling, NO knob, NO spore and NO capsule anywhere on the cell. It is a small compact rod, not a long filament and not a sphere.

STREAMING FROM ONE POLE ONLY is the organism's signature: a COMET TAIL of HOST ACTIN FILAMENTS, rendered as a DENSE FIBROUS MAT of many hundreds of individually resolved fine strands — like a matted brush, a felted bundle of hair, a thicket of fine roots — criss-crossing and branching, packed tight where they meet the pole and fraying into loose separate strands at the far end. The tail is about one and a half times the bacterium's length and fans out wider than the bacterium. Give the strands their own visibly separate three-dimensional relief so it reads as a tangle of real filaments in the electron beam. It must NOT be a smooth solid rudder, a single whip or flagellum, a flame, a plume of smoke, a glow, or straight radiating rays. NO radiating straight lines, speed lines or starburst anywhere.

Also visible: TWO or THREE very fine, long, smoothly wavy FLAGELLA springing from the sides and the opposite pole and trailing across the substrate — thin smooth single threads, clearly distinct from the matted fibrous tail.

FALSE-COLOUR PALETTE: the bacterium in a warm butter-gold to soft amber; the actin comet tail in a distinctly COOL PALE BLUE-WHITE so it reads as a different material from the cell; the substrate a muted cool teal-grey with soft fibrous texture suggesting the inside of a host cell. Rich but restrained false colour, of the kind added digitally to a real SEM plate.

Surface only — an SEM shows no interior, which is correct here: no cutaway, no visible nucleoid or ribosomes.

Fill the whole square edge to edge. No black border, no dark frame, no vignette, no letterbox bars, no sheet-on-a-surface look. No text, no letters, no numbers, no labels, no scale bar, no instrument data band, no watermark. A single specimen only, no duplicates.
